questions.question: What is the main axis vs the cross axis in Flexbox?
questions.answer: The main axis is set by flex-direction (row = horizontal, column = vertical). The cross axis is perpendicular. justify-content works on the main axis; align-items/align-content work on the cross axis.

questions.question: Explain justify-content and align-content differences.
questions.answer: justify-content distributes items along the main axis. align-content distributes wrapped lines along the cross axis and has no effect on a single-line container. align-items aligns items within a line.

questions.question: How do flex-grow, flex-shrink, and flex-basis work together?
questions.answer: flex-basis is the starting size, flex-grow controls how extra free space is distributed, and flex-shrink controls how overflow is reduced. flex: 1 = 1 1 0%, flex: auto = 1 1 auto, flex: none = 0 0 auto.

questions.question: Why does a flex item refuse to shrink below its content?
questions.answer: The default min-width:auto on flex items prevents shrinking below the content's minimum size. Set min-width:0 (or overflow:hidden) on the item to allow truncation/shrinking.

questions.question: Does order change accessibility or keyboard order?
questions.answer: No. order changes visual order only; the DOM order still drives tab order and screen-reader reading order. Use it for minor visual adjustments, not meaningful reordering.

questions.question: Create a sidebar + content layout with a fixed 240px sidebar.
Why does flex:1 behave differently from flex:auto?
questions.answer: flex:1 sets basis to 0%, so all flexible items start equal and split space evenly regardless of content. flex:auto uses basis auto, so items start from their content size before growing.

questions.question: Why do margins not collapse between flex items?
questions.answer: Flex containers establish a flex formatting context, where margin collapsing does not apply. Use gap for spacing instead of relying on margin collapse.
